dedupe_keys.name: nasa race runtime for airspace concept evaluation open source distributed actor framework for live air traffic data and simulation systems

description: RACE is a NASA Ames open-source software framework for configurable, highly concurrent and distributed message-based systems, first built to evaluate airspace concepts, listed in the NASA Software Catalog (case ARC-17749-1). Contents: a distributed actor system running in Java virtual machines that gives one programming model for point-to-point and publish-subscribe messaging within a process, between processes and between machines, with uniform configuration and deterministic initialisation and termination; it is used to build simulations spanning several machines with synchronised displays, to interface existing hardware simulators and other live data feeds, and to include visualisation components such as NASA's WorldWind viewer. Producer: NASA Ames; the catalogue lists version 1.0 from January 2016 for Windows, Linux and macOS. Coverage: generic. Format and access: open source release with source code and documentation pages linked from the catalogue. Licence: NASA open source release (terms in the repository). Caveats: a development framework, not a ready model, so data feeds and simulation components must be supplied or configured. Simulation uses: building live digital twins of airspace and airport operations, fusing operational data feeds for disruption monitoring, and coupling simulators with visualisation. Related records: NASA MFSim (platform-multi-fidelity-simulator-mfsim) is another NASA air traffic simulation environment.
